content.text: Problem: When cross-cutting concerns are embedded into business logic, it leads to tight coupling, reducing modularity and making the code harder to maintain.
AOP is a programming paradigm that separates cross-cutting concerns from business logic, making code cleaner and more maintainable.
Logging is embedded, creating tight coupling.
Logging is separated into an aspect. Business logic is cleaner.

rows: A class that encapsulates a cross-cutting concern (annotated with @Aspect).

Code to be executed at a join point (e.g., logging, security).
Expression to match join points (i.e., where to apply advice).
Runs if method throws an exception.
Runs after method ends, regardless of exception.
Runs before and after method execution.

items: aspectjweaver: Enables AOP weaving at runtime.
Separation of concerns – Business logic is isolated from cross-cutting concerns.
Maintainability – Easy to update or replace concerns (e.g., change logging framework).
Cleaner code – Less clutter in core business logic.
